title: Nearby Places Search
summary: Find restaurants, shops, and landmarks within a radius or map viewport at global scale.
statement:
Design a location search backend that powers 'near me' discovery for a maps and local-business app.

Functional requirements:
- Given a user's latitude, longitude, search radius (for example `500 m` to `20 km`), and optional category filter, return matching places ranked by distance and rating.
- Business owners add new places and update opening hours, addresses, or closures.
- Support viewing full details for any selected place.

Scale to assume:
- 250 million registered places worldwide, unevenly distributed between dense city centers and rural areas.
- 500,000 nearby search queries per second.
- Only a few thousand business profile updates per second; edits may take a few minutes to appear in search.
hints: Why does `WHERE lat BETWEEN ... AND lng BETWEEN ...` on two standard database columns perform poorly at 500,000 QPS, and how do spatial indexes map 2D coordinates into partitionable cells?
A user standing right next to a cell boundary can be closer to a cafe in the neighboring cell than to anything in their own cell. How does your query handle edges and varying urban density?
Compare the size of the whole world's `(place_id, lat, lng, category)` index against RAM on a single server.
expectations: Clarifies read-to-write asymmetry, eventual consistency tolerance for business edits, category filtering, and radius versus bounding-box queries.
Sizes the compact spatial dataset (250M places fit in tens of gigabytes of RAM), showing why the spatial index can be replicated in memory across search replicas.
Compares geohashes, S2/H3 hierarchical cells, and dynamic quadtrees, addressing dense urban hotspots versus sparse oceans/rural regions.
Queries the target cell plus surrounding neighbor cells (or expands quadtree nodes) to avoid missing closer places across cell boundaries, then filters exact Haversine distance and ranks.
Separates the lightweight spatial index from the richer place-details store, caching popular place records and cells by region.
Applies business creates and edits to a durable source-of-truth database and streams incremental updates or periodic rebuilds to the spatial replicas.
Deploys regional replicas close to users and handles open-now filtering using local time zones and structured operating hours.
